__
 
• Let's look at the use of the given words:
 
 
• We use **When **to refer to a future situation or condition that we are certain of, whereas we use if to introduce a possible or unreal situation.
 
• “**What**” is an interrogative pronoun. This means it stand for something the speaker does not yet know.
 
• We use **Where **as a conjunction meaning **'in the place that'** or **'in situations that'**. The clause with where is a subordinate clause and needs a main clause to complete its meaning.
 
• We use **That **to introduce defining relative clauses. We can use that instead of who, whom or which to refer to people, animals and things.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence **'Sarnath'** is a place and we know to denote a place,** 'Where'** should be used.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2.**

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: them

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Let's look at the use of the given **pronouns**.

 
 
• "**Them**" is used as the object of a verb or preposition. We use **them **to refer to a group of people, animals, or things.
 
• "They" is used to indicate a nonbinary or gender-neutral subject (doer) of a verb (action) instead of he or she.
 
• "He" is a singular pronoun. It is a word that takes the place of a singular noun when the person is of masculine gender.
 
• "We" is the first person plural pronoun. We is used as the subject of a verb and before a noun to make it clear which group of people you are referring to.
 
 
 
• The usage of **“Let they”** is incorrect whereas **“Let them”** is grammatically correct. 

Therefore the correct answer is option 1.

Complete sentence: *The police will let **them **__go after seeing their passes.*​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **__Confusion Points__**

 
• **They** and **them **are always used in place of plural nouns or noun groups in the third person.
 
• However, the fundamental difference between the two in grammatical terms, is that **they** is a subject pronoun, and **them **is an object pronoun.
 
• **They **is used to refer to the subject of a clause.

• A comma (,) is added after the direct speech part.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3) i.e. 'it affects many body functions.' [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The **first** sentence of the **second and third** paragraphs mentions that "paediatric multi-system inflammatory syndrome."
 
• In this context, the meaning of ‘multi-system disorder’ is that 'its is a rare but fatal illness in which the heart, lungs, kidneys, brain, skin, eyes, or gastrointestinal organs can be inflamed due to COVID-19.'
 
• Therefore from the above sentence, we can certainly say that it affects multiple organs of the human body.
 
• Hence, the only possible answer is option 3.

questions.question: **The word ‘paediatric’ in the passage refers to:**
questions.solution: The correct answer is option 3) i.e. 'medical care of children.' [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] <span style="vertical-align: middle;font-size: 21px;"&

questions.question: **When the City Mayor says, "We are now on high alert in addressing the syndrome”, he means:**

options.text: people are consulting each other in panic
the city administration is concerned about war
the administration understands it’s an urgent health issue
it’s sad for the people who are suffering

questions.solution: The correct answer is option 3) i.e. 'the administration understands it’s an urgent health issue.'
